Welcome to

At the intersection of algorithms, data and discovery, KhaledLab seeks to harness the power of Artificial Intelligence to solve some of the most pressing challenges in science and society. Based in the Department of Computer Science at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (SIUC) and led by Dr. Khaled Mohammed Saifuddin, our group explores how intelligent systems can be made more robust, efficient, and interpretable. We focus on graph machine learning, graph mining, and Network Science, developing new methods for complex and heterogeneous network representation. These advances are applied across diverse domains, from bioinformatics, health data analysis to sequence and event understanding, vision-language reasoning tasks. By bridging fundamental theory with real-world impact, KhaledLab pushes the boundaries of AI toward creating knowledge that is not only powerful, but transformative.

See our publications Join the lab Latest news
  • New Surface Cues Over Structure: Probing LLM Behavior on Brain Connectivity Graphs accepted at IEEE Big Data 2026. Congratulations Prapti on her first first-author PhD work! 🎉
  • New Does Graph Compression Preserve Signal Propagation? accepted at IEEE ICMLA 2026. Congratulations Kawshik on his first first-author PhD work! 🎉
Research areas Graph AI

Advancing graph and hypergraph neural networks, graph GenAI with a focus on robustness, efficiency, and interpretability.

Graph Mining and Network Science

Discovering patterns, communities, and dynamics in large-scale, complex heterogeneous networks.

AI for Biomedicine

Applying graph-based AI to drug discovery, drug repurposing, bioinformatics, and health data analytics.

Sequence and Multimodal Learning

Modeling sequential, temporal, and multimodal data for event prediction, genomics, and vision–language reasoning.

docs.title: Director
docs.text:
Dr. Khaled Mohammed Saifuddin Tenure-track Assistant Professor, Computer Science School of Computing, Southern Illinois University Carbondale (Carnegie R1) 📧 k.saifuddin@siu.edu 🏢 EGRA 409E Google Scholar LinkedIn ResearchGate About

Before joining Southern Illinois University Carbondale, Dr. Khaled Mohammed Saifuddin served as a Postdoctoral Research Associate at the Barabási Lab under Albert-László Barabási and earned his Ph.D. in Computer Science from Georgia State University under Dr. Esra Akbas.

His research has been published in top venues such as ICDE, CIKM, ECML PKDD, DSAA, ACM-BCB, IJCNN, PRICAI, IEEE BigData and KDD workshops and presented at the Stanford Graph Learning Workshop. He has held leadership roles as Area Chair for AI4Science–ICML and NeurIPS. He is the recipient of the Outstanding Poster Presentation Award at the Machine Learning in Drug Discovery Symposium 2023 at the Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard.

Selected professional activities
  • Served as a Mentor at the LogML 2026 Summer School on Geometry and Machine Learning, London.
  • Chaired the Special Session 'Graph Machine Learning for Complex Systems and Applications' at ICMLA 2026.
  • Co-chaired the Special Session 'Advances in Multimodal AI: Method and Application' at SMC 2026.
  • Organized the SNAS Interdisciplinary Research Conference 2026.

docs.title: Opportunities
docs.text:
⚠️ Currently No PhD Positions Available

We are not currently recruiting PhD students. However, Masters and Undergraduate students at SIUC who are interested in our research areas are encouraged to contact the Lab Director.

🎓 Fully Funded PhD Positions in Computer Science

Southern Illinois University, Carbondale (SIUC) • Starting Spring 2026 and beyond

Join KhaledLab at SIUC — an R1 Carnegie Classification institution recognized for outstanding research excellence.

We are looking for highly motivated Ph.D. students in Computer Science to work on cutting-edge topics in:

  • Graph Machine Learning, Graph GenAI, Graph Mining, Network Science
  • Bioinformatics, Network Medicine, Health Data Analytics
  • Visual and Language Reasoning, Event Understanding, Social Network Analysis

This position offers a unique chance to contribute to both theoretical advancements— developing new algorithms, models, and frameworks and applied research, where these innovations will be leveraged to address real-world challenges in science, medicine, and technology. Students will gain hands-on experience with cutting-edge AI methods while also building cross-disciplinary collaborations that maximize both scientific impact and career development.

Basic Requirements
  • BS/MS in Computer Science or related fields
  • Strong programming skills (Python, PyTorch, C, C++)
  • Solid understanding of machine learning and deep learning fundamentals
  • Excellent analytical thinking and problem-solving skills
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work independently and in collaborative teams
Desired Qualifications
  • Familiarity with Graph AI and Generative AI
  • Experience in publishing research papers
  • Hands-on experience with transformer models or large language models (LLMs) is a plus
How to Apply

Send the following documents to Dr. Khaled Mohammed Saifuddin:

  • CV
  • Transcript
  • GRE (mandatory)
  • English Test Scores

In the subject line, add: 'Prospective PhD Student'

📧 k.saifuddin@siu.edu 📢 For SIUC Students

Any Masters or Undergraduate student at SIUC who is interested in our research areas is encouraged to contact the Lab director.

docs.title: Research
docs.text:
Ongoing projects Graph AI Graph Mining & Network Science AI for Biomedicine Sequence & Multimodal Learning Ongoing projects

Current lab projects supported by the NSF National AI Research Resource (NAIRR) Pilot.

NSF NAIRR Pilot 14,000 GPU hours · NCSA Delta RelGuard: Closing the Relational Gap in Adversarial Defenses for Large Vision-Language Models

Large vision-language models can be misled by tiny, invisible changes to an image. RelGuard studies how such attacks disrupt a model’s understanding of the relationships within a scene, and develops a defense and an evaluation protocol that keep that understanding intact.

Read the announcement NSF NAIRR Pilot 2,965 GPU hours · PSC Bridges-2 Long-Range Biological Reasoning with Hypergraph Foundation Models

Many biological effects come from groups of genes, drugs, and molecules acting together. This project builds foundation-scale hypergraph neural networks that capture these group interactions and long-range network structure across genes, diseases, drugs, pathways, side effects, and the microbiome.

Read the announcement Graph AI

Advancing graph and hypergraph neural networks and graph GenAI, with a focus on robustness, efficiency, and interpretability.

Surface Cues Over Structure: Probing LLM Behavior on Brain Connectivity Graphs BigData 2026LLMs on GraphsBrain Networks

Can LLMs actually reason over brain connectivity graphs? Through a controlled study of ADHD diagnosis from resting-state fMRI connectivity, this work shows that six LLMs, from small open-weight models to a recent proprietary one, follow surface cues such as region names, number formatting, and prompt framing rather than the subject’s connectivity.

How it worksEach subject’s rs-fMRI is turned into a brain graph, with brain regions as nodes and functional connectivity as edges, and given to the LLM as text. Five probes then test the knowledge source, statistical context, structure identification, perturbation sensitivity, and whether the model’s justifications match the data.

HyperGCL: Multi-Modal Graph Contrastive Learning via Learnable Hypergraph Views IJCNN 2025Hypergraph GCLMultimodal LearningAdaptive Augmentation

HyperGCL constructs three complementary hypergraph views from structure and attributes, then applies a learnable, topology-aware augmentation. A network-aware contrastive loss aligns the views while preserving important relations and filtering noise.

How it worksSystem architecture of HyperGCL. Three hypergraph views are built from the input graph and node attributes, a learnable augmentation generates adaptive views, view-specific encoders learn each view, and a network-aware contrastive loss is combined with a supervised loss to train the model.

Topology-Guided Hypergraph Transformer Network: Unveiling Structural Insights for Improved Representation PRICAI 2025Stanford Graph Learning Workshop 2024Graph TransformerStructure-Aware Attention

THTN represents subgraphs as hyperedges to capture higher-order relations, and uses a structure-aware attention that jointly weighs semantic and topological cues. A structural–spatial encoding module adds graph topology and spatial context to node embeddings, capturing both local and global dependencies.

How it worksTHTN combines structural and spatial encoding, which enriches node features, with structure-aware attention, which brings the structural importance of nodes and hyperedges into attribute-based semantic attention.

Graph Mining & Network Science

Discovering patterns, communities, and dynamics in large-scale, complex, heterogeneous networks.

Does Graph Compression Preserve Signal Propagation? ICMLA 2026Graph CompressionOversmoothing

Graph compression makes graph learning cheaper, but does it keep how signals spread through the graph? Studying coarsening and sparsification across five datasets, this work finds a consistent trade-off: coarsening follows the original propagation more faithfully but oversmooths more, while sparsification keeps signals diverse but drifts further from the original as depth grows.

How it worksNode features are propagated on the original and compressed graphs at increasing depths, and the two are compared using deviation from the original trajectory, Dirichlet energy, and numeric rank. The figure shows the deviation for coarsening (dashed) and sparsification (solid) methods.

Enhancing GNN Representations via Homophily-Aware Subgraphs with Multi-Objective Learning DSAA 2026k-trussSubgraph Contrastive Learning

GNNs lose information when signals from different classes mix during long-range propagation. HASCL splits the graph into tightly connected k-truss subgraphs, which keep strong homophily, and learns node representations that stay consistent with their own subgraph. It outperforms 15 baselines on node classification across eight homophilic and heterophilic datasets.

How it worksThe graph is decomposed into k-truss subgraphs; a GCN learns node embeddings and SAGPool learns subgraph embeddings. Positive and negative subgraph views, made by shifting subgraph indices or adding RealNVP-based noise, drive a contrastive loss that is trained jointly with a supervised loss.

Tackling Oversmoothing in GNN via Graph Sparsification ECML PKDD 2024Truss-based PruningOversmoothing

TGS uses truss decomposition to prune redundant edges from dense graph regions. This preserves essential topological structure while preventing the excessive feature mixing that causes oversmoothing in deep GNNs.

How it worksTruss decomposition-based edge pruning framework for graph sparsification to tackle oversmoothing.

AI for Biomedicine

Applying graph-based AI to drug discovery, drug repurposing, bioinformatics, and health data analytics.

Fin-H2AN: Fingerprint-based Heterogeneous Hypergraph Attention Network for Molecular Property Prediction DSAA 2026Molecular FingerprintsHeterogeneous Hypergraph

Fin-H2AN predicts molecular properties by placing all molecules and the substructures from three molecular fingerprints (MACCS, ErG, and PubChem) into one heterogeneous hypergraph. This captures higher-order relations between molecules that standard GNNs miss, and it achieves the best average rank against state-of-the-art models on MoleculeNet benchmarks.

How it worksEach fingerprint bit becomes a node and each molecule becomes a hyperedge connecting its active bits. A dual attention network first passes molecular context to the fingerprint nodes, then gathers the most relevant nodes of each fingerprint type into a molecule embedding for prediction.

HeTAN: Heterogeneous Graph Triplet Attention Network for Drug Repurposing DSAA 2024Drug RepurposingTriplet Attention

HeTAN models interactions among drugs, targets, and diseases together. Triplet message passing and triplet-wise attention capture higher-order relationships beyond pairwise links, uncovering meaningful drug–target–disease associations.

How it worksHeTAN builds a heterogeneous network of drug, target, and disease nodes, learns node representations with triplet message passing and triplet-wise attention, and predicts drug–target–disease interactions with an MLP.

HyGNN: Drug-Drug Interaction Prediction via Hypergraph Neural Network ICDE 2023Drug–Drug InteractionHyperGNN

HyGNN predicts drug–drug interactions from SMILES alone by building a hypergraph of molecular substructures. It outperforms baselines on F1, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC and generalizes to new, unseen drugs.

How it worksHyGNN builds a hypergraph where each drug is a hyperedge and frequent chemical substructures are nodes, then learns drug representations with an attention-based hyperedge encoder and predicts interactions with a decoder.

Drug Abuse Detection in Twitter-sphere: Graph-Based Approach BigData 2021Health Data AnalyticsText Graphs

This work detects drug abuse events on social media by building corpus- and document-level text graphs from Twitter data. GNN-based models outperform traditional machine learning and deep learning approaches at identifying drug abuse-related content.

How it worksGraph-based drug abuse detection: data collection and preprocessing, corpus- and document-level text graph construction, and GNN-based classification of drug abuse-related tweets.

Effects of COVID-19 on Individuals in Opioid Addiction Recovery ICMLA 2021Health Data AnalyticsSocial Media

Analyzing Twitter data, this study finds a 30% drop in medication-assisted treatment (MAT) use and more mentions of illicit opioids during COVID-19, highlighting relapse risks and the need for continued care.

How it worksFive-step framework for analyzing the impact of COVID-19 on active MAT medicine users using Twitter data.

Sequence & Multimodal Learning

Modeling sequential, temporal, and multimodal data for event prediction, genomics, and vision–language reasoning.

DyGCL: Dynamic Graph Contrastive Learning for Event Prediction BigData 2024Dynamic GNNEvent Prediction

DyGCL captures both fine-grained node dynamics and the overall structural evolution of a graph through local and global view encoders. Contrastive learning and attention-based fusion let it model temporal patterns effectively across real-world datasets.

How it worksDyGCL feeds dynamic graphs into a local-view encoder (dynamic node representations) and a global-view encoder (graph pooling with an LSTM), aligns them with contrastive learning, and combines them for event prediction.

Seq-HyGAN: Sequence Classification via Hypergraph Attention Network CIKM 2023Sequence AnalysisHyperGNN

Seq-HyGAN models higher-order relationships among subsequences for sequence classification. Attention-based learning captures both local and global dependencies, producing richer representations than existing approaches.

How it worksSeq-HyGAN builds a hypergraph where each sequence (e.g., DNA) is a hyperedge and frequent subsequences are nodes, then learns sequence representations with attention on the important subsequences.
